scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Dispute ticket volume increased from about 610 in June and 590 in July to 1,180 in August and 1,260 in September, showing roughly a doubling since August.
Route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, with 9,200 manual read accounts, indicating field operations are falling short of the expected read collection rate.
The observation shows disputed bills for both estimated (1,240) and actual (1,785) reads, with actual reads higher. This indicates the dispute surge is not limited to estimated‑read bills.
Dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days < SLA 3.0 days) with 2,440 tickets, indicating response speed is adequate and not a primary driver of the dispute surge.
The tariff change log contains no records, indicating that no tariff changes have been recorded in the billing system during the period under review.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder claims there has been no tariff change this year, indicating tariff changes are not a cause of the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field team reports a shortage of three meter readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in more estimated bills for affected customers.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that route priority changes require Field Operations Manager confirmation, aligning with the existing dispatch approval constraint.

E-09.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned, enabling retrieval of AMI read events that were previously blocked by pending access.

Among disputed estimated bills, a large subset (1184) had AMI reads taken before the billing cutoff that were rejected due to high consumption, while a smaller subset (56) had no AMI read received, indicating that read rejections—not missing reads—contribute to estimated bills.

symptoms: Dispute ticket volume doubled since August
problem_definition.root_problem: Insufficient field meter reading capacity due to staffing shortage causes incomplete manual read collection, leading to increased reliance on estimated bills and consequently higher dispute ticket volume.

trace.summary: Insufficient field meter reading capacity due to staffing shortage causes incomplete manual read collection, leading to increased reliance on estimated bills and consequently higher dispute ticket volume.

Because hiring additional readers cannot be completed within the remaining 225‑minute contest window, an AI agent is needed to provide immediate dispute ticket responses and reduce backlog while the structural remedies are enacted.

structural_remedies.description: Hire or contract three additional meter readers to address the staffing shortage (E-07, CL-03). This is expected to raise route completion from the current 0.88 (E-02) toward the 0.95 target, as increasing headcount is assumed to improve completion (A-A4).
structural_remedies.rationale: Hiring and onboarding likely exceed the remaining 225‑minute window.; residual gap: Even with added readers, route completion may still be affected by routing inefficiencies or non‑manual read accounts, leaving a small gap to the 0.95 target.

structural_remedies.description: Modify billing import logic to prioritize AMI register reads (DA-MDMS) and lower the estimate‑substitution threshold. This reduces reliance on estimated bills, which are a primary driver of dispute tickets (E-03, E-01).
structural_remedies.rationale: Configuration change can be completed within remaining minutes and does not involve automated bill writes.; residual gap: Accounts without AMI coverage will continue to generate estimated bills, so some dispute volume may persist until those meters are upgraded or manual reads improve.

solution_design.why_agent: Because hiring additional readers cannot be completed within the remaining 225‑minute contest window, an AI agent is needed to provide immediate dispute ticket responses and reduce backlog while the structural remedies are enacted.
solution_design.bridge_sunset_condition: When three additional meter readers are hired and onboarded, and route completion rate reaches >=0.95.
